Subject: Post-demo recap + stakeholder/gatekeeper map request

Hi Elena / Carlos —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can align the next steps with your procurement and security gates: 

Recap (very short):
- You liked the predictable p95 latency for short-chat workflows and the Dedicated capacity isolation.
- Main concerns: procurement timeline (legal + SSO/KMS review), and whether a Private VPC deployment is required for PHI data in production.

Can you confirm the following so we can put together an accurate mutual action plan?
1) Economic buyer / approver: who signs and what thresholds require exec sign-off?
2) Procurement owner / legal reviewer: name and preferred procurement cadence (standard 30–45 day review or longer?)
3) Security contact (for SOC2/infra questions and KMS/HSM integration) — would you like us to share our security snapshot and run a workshop?
4) Target p95 latency and cost envelope for the PoC and a sample production Q3 run-rate (ballpark numbers are fine)
5) Deployment preference: Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), or Private (VPC/on-prem)? If Private, is there an internal infra team we should sync with?

Attachments: I added a one-pager that contrasts Hosted vs Private paths and our security snapshot. Also attaching a simple spreadsheet template you can fill with names/owners if that helps.

Proposed next steps:
- If you can confirm the owners above, we’ll draft a Mutual Action Plan and propose dates for a procurement kickoff + security workshop.
- Tentative timeline: procurement kickoff (week of May 10), security workshop (mid-May), contract draft (late May).

Ben & Karthik — looping you for any redlines or notes on SLA wording/hosted fallbacks.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + stakeholder/gatekeeper map request

Thanks Camila — great demo. Quick answers inline below and a couple of asks.

1) Economic buyer / approver: Laura Hsu (VP of Product) signs anything > $100k annually. Below that the procurement director can approve. I’ll loop Laura if we see >$100k run-rate.
2) Procurement owner / legal reviewer: That’s me and James Liu (I copied him). Typical cadence is 3–6 weeks but security findings can extend that.
3) Security contact: James will own the security checklist; he asked if you can provide a SOC2 report and a short note on KMS/HSM integrations.
4) Target p95 latency: For chat assistant flows we’re targeting p95 <= 250ms for requests under 256 tokens during peak hours. Cost envelope for PoC: <$10k for the first month (experimentation budget). Production: TBD — likely to scale to ~4–6x PoC.
5) Deployment preference: We’re leaning Dedicated initially (predictable throughput + isolation) but may require Private for PHI scope later. If we go Private, our infra lead is James (looped).

One more thing — procurement will need a simple statement of rollback/fallthrough: if Dedicated capacity underperforms we need an SLA on fallback to another model or region. Can you draft suggested SLA language?

Thanks —
Elena
Director of Partnerships | HealthBridge AI
elena.soto@healthbridge.ai

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + stakeholder/gatekeeper map request

Looping in a couple internal notes and proposed SLA language for Elena/James to consider.

Internal notes: 
- If HealthBridge wants Dedicated for PoC and possible Private later, recommended path: start Hosted (thin) for early integration work, flip to Dedicated for controlled load testing, then run Private pilot only if PHI scope requires it. This reduces procurement time and gives measurable perf data.
- For Dedicated p95 guarantees we can offer an SLO-backed target with credits for missed p95 thresholds; exact credit schedule depends on commit level.

Proposed SLA snippet (draft):
"Redwood will maintain a 95th percentile latency (p95) not exceeding 300ms for standard chat workloads (requests <= 256 tokens) when serving from Dedicated capacity during normal operating conditions. In the event Redwood fails to meet the p95 target for a contiguous 1-hour window due to capacity or software issues, Redwood will: (a) notify HealthBridge; (b) automatically route new requests to a pre-agreed fallback model variant or alternate region to preserve availability; and (c) issue service credit equivalent to X% of the monthly committed fee for the affected hour(s), up to a monthly cap."

Questions for HealthBridge (to confirm):
- Is the PoC acceptance gate based on p95 only, or do you require head-to-head quality parity checks versus your current baseline?
- Can Elena or James confirm the procurement timeline (3–6 weeks) and whether a PO will be required for the PoC spend?

Camila — I attached the security snapshot and one-pager again to the thread for easy reference. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the SLA language.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
